Body cam: police use taser on mentally ill patient, who dies five days later

ATHENS, ALABAMA — Police released body cam footage of an incident at Athens Limestone Hospital on Feb. 3, where cops tased a mentally ill patient that later died.

Paramedics were trying to administer a mental health evaluation to Randy Nelson, but Nelson was not cooperating. The cops try to calm him down, but Nelson could not be controlled, and was not able to be reasoned with.

After continued attempts to help restrain Nelson proved unsuccessful, the officers resorted to using a taser. Sgt. Greg Lott continued to tase Nelson until he stopped moving. The officers then handcuffed him, and helped hospital staff strap him onto a stretcher and transport him to another room.

Unfortunately, the charge used on him may have been too much, because he struggled to breathe from that point on. Randy Nelson died five days later.

Now, an investigation has been launched into whether an excessive amount of force was used to subdue the patient. An autopsy report is pending, and a confirmed cause of death has yet to be determined.
